chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī, from Fuḍayl al-Rassān, from Raqabah ibn Maṣqalah, who said:

I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and asked him about some matters. He said: “I see that you are among those who give fatwa in the mosque of al-ʿIrāq.” I said: “Yes.” He said to me: “From whom are you?” I said: “A cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.” He said: “Welcome to you, O cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.”

So I said to him: “What do you say regarding wiping over the khuffs?” He said: “ʿUmar used to hold it to be for three days for the traveler and one day and one night for the resident, while my father did not hold it to be valid whether in travel or in residence.”

Then when I came out from his presence and stood on the threshold of the door, he said to me: “Come forward, O cousin of Ṣaʿṣaʿah.” So I came toward him, and he said: “Those people used to speak according to their own opinion, so they would err and be correct, while my father did not speak according to his own opinion.”

key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: the two leather socks or foot-coverings
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping, here in the context of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.بِرَأْيِهِمْ: according to their own opinion or personal reasoning

ai.seo_question: What does Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say about wiping over the khuffs in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a discussion with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the ruling of wiping over the khuffs in wudu (ablution). The Imam contrasts a known ruling attributed to ʿUmar with the position of his father, and then emphasizes that others used personal opinion, whereas his father did not speak from personal opinion.
